plotEn:
The film begins with a scene in the Tarapith cremation ground some thousand years before the 19th century, where sage Vasishtha is engaged in tantric sadhana at the panchamundi seat. Goddess Tara is pleased by his devotion and shows up. She tells him that in the later ages, a sadhak will achieve "siddhi" (enlightenment) at the very seat he (Vasistha) is seated on and carry forward the glory of Tarapith. This is where one of the many "most holy" temples of Goddess Parvati, is situated.
In the 19th century, near the cremation ground at Atla village, the wife of the Brahmin priest Sarvananda Chattopadhyay has a stillborn child. Through Goddess Tara's blessing, the child lives, and he is named Bamacharan, and Sarvananda "offers" him to Goddess Tara. Bama grows referring to Goddess Tara as his "Boro Maa" ("Greater Mother"), and that his biological mother "Choto Maa" (Smaller Mother, here on the idea that she's a mere earthly being compared to the Goddess of Time, Tara, Herself).
He spends his childhood assisting his father, who earns a living by singing and worshipping Goddess Tara. However, unlike his father, Bama mentions multiple time that he feels spiritual connection with his "Boro Maa", even though he has never seen her. His speaking to Goddess Tara and doing certain actions which Baman insists were Her instructions results in people around him believing he's delusional and somewhat of unsound mind ("Khyapa", hence the name "Bamakhyapa" or "Bama the mad").
